approach.method_basis: The Parent maintains the best 64 scored molecular graphs and draws breeding parents from preferred score quantiles. It builds a fresh pool through fragment crossover and short chains of atom or bond mutations, then uses a Gaussian process on count fingerprints to choose which molecules receive scores. Correlated posterior draws select a batch; after three batches without a new best score, selection is restricted to the forty highest predicted means. Its ordinary mutation choices do not learn which edit works on a particular source molecule.
approach.novelty: Replace that ordinary mutation chain with an accepted-success fragment editor. A graph network learns where to add a fragment, which fragment fits that site, or which directed branch to delete, using only its own purchased edits that improve on their original source. This differs from earlier frequency-only motifs, fixed context substitutions, parent-success weights and predictor changes: the learned object is the exact source-conditioned construction action. The crossover and purchase-selection mechanisms remain the host for this single change.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de has complete Search mean 0.607030316211131 (SD 0.030175277546149237), yet its ordinary single-parent route spends most purchases on edits that do not improve their source. A read-only audit of all fifteen archived Search sessions joins every emitted identity to accepted feedback, prior real source scores and trajectories: only 429 of 2870 ordinary purchases beat their source; equal-session positive raw source gain per paid ordinary molecule is 0.003968522922923545, falling to 0.0019826746921883824 over the late scope (162 beats among 1477 ordinary purchases). The source records are frozen in policy/scratch/r0075-00-improve-L01/evidence-review.json and its fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files, with underlying log/trajectory/summary/run hashes. n-61cb8ba305fa's correction removal restores these exact trajectories despite a lower passive mixture MSE; it is not an independent replication of the Parent. n-814ee0b4f000 constructed and bought 746 frequency-only motif products but lost 0.053376 and diluted crossover: supply without source/site conditioning is insufficient in that tested recipe. n-030a6ccbba7c on its different binary-GP Development Parent shifted parent draws and increased small improvement counts while losing 0.02157946287432137. These are scoped contrary variants, not a proof that any learned editor will fail. The testable bottleneck is the absence of feedback-trained source/site/fragment construction in the ordinary route, with useful paid source-gain transfer left to this experiment.

adoptions.applicability: n-61cb8ba305fa resolves the recent calibration-to-endpoint mismatch without repairing uneven core/linker access. n-814ee0b4f000 proves coarse products can be constructed and purchased but frequency-only, site-unconditioned supply loses 0.053376 and dilutes crossover. n-030a6ccbba7c shows source-level success weights buy more small wins without better endpoints. The new mechanism learns which site/fragment or directed cut to propose from the molecular source and its exact successful edit; it preserves crossover exposure and does not rename either old credit rule.

method_change.previous_method: The code Parent's fixed one/two/three-call ordinary primitive-mutation chain, within score-ranked graph evolution and count-GP posterior selection.
method_change.proposed_method: One bounded source-conditioned fragment add/delete action learned by exact-action maximum likelihood from strictly source-improving real purchases, with the original chain as its declared failure fallback.
method_change.rationale: The actual Parent audit shows weak ordinary-route source gains, while the indexed motif and parent-credit experiments show that coarse supply or more small source wins alone does not ensure useful search. A learned conditional construction action is distinct and testable on this host without replacing its GP or diluting crossover.

hypothesis: Modify the ordinary single-parent proposal mechanism of n-cf8d309c06de into one session-local, source-conditioned fragment add/delete editor. A six-iteration 64-dimensional graph encoder assigns masked addition-site, site-conditioned-fragment and directed-deletion probabilities; positive exact policy edits enter likelihood replay only after real purchase and strict improvement over their original real scored source. Full action MLE changes later construction probabilities while the inherited GP still chooses purchases. The causal prediction is that activated learned construction increases equal-session positive raw source gain per paid ordinary-route molecule, including its fallback and zero-gain outcomes; endpoint gain is a separate consequence to test.

finding_summary.headline: Learned edits raise ordinary-route source gains by 25%, but final score falls by 0.0497
finding_summary.insights: This separates successful learning from successful optimization: real improvements over a generating source can train a molecular editor and increase average local gains without reliably advancing the best molecule. The full-period gain is not an all-session or late-period benefit: eight sessions improve and seven decline. The action distribution becomes sharply concentrated. Duplicate attempts rise from 48.2% early to 82.8% late, live-source entropy falls from about 6.97 to 1.87 nats, and 14.6% of ordinary opportunities exhaust twelve attempts and use the original fallback. These observations point to a novelty-aware proposal or search method that can vary connected cores and linkers while preserving useful context, rather than further rewarding already successful edits. The chemistry supports that diagnosis without showing universal scaffold collapse: small fragments and very large assemblies both become more common, while one poorly scoring high region covers only five generic scaffolds versus ten in the Parent and loses much of its saturated ring-amine coverage. Other sessions still reach diverse ring amines and aryl nitriles, so those groups are available. The tested adapter’s endpoint contribution is negative under this host, but the experiment does not isolate the effects of vocabulary, architecture and positive-only replay, and it does not settle the broader learned-editor approach.
finding_summary.results: The registered full-period prediction passed. Across all fifteen sessions, positive source gain per paid ordinary-route molecule rose from 0.003969 to 0.004970, a 25.25% increase. The denominator includes all 2424 ordinary purchases, including 730 fallbacks and every zero-gain or untrained purchase; the Parent had 2870 ordinary purchases. Learning used 354 real source-improving policy edits, made 10475 gradient updates, increased same-record log likelihood by an equal-session average 0.3163 nats per training block, and changed the probability of 1286 later paid actions. Directed-cut choices learned in every session; one session had no successful additions and kept uniform addition heads. All 4350 purchases completed. The benefit did not persist late: source gain fell from the Parent’s 0.001983 to 0.001812, and late ordinary incumbent-gain mass fell from 0.7179 to 0.1782. Final mean Top-1 fell from 0.607030 to 0.557296, with all three seed means lower. Seven task/seed endpoints improved and eight declined; sitagliptin had a material paired regression. Thus the mechanism is confirmed on its registered source-gain test, while the endpoint target failed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heteroaromatics and aryl amines, with useful nitriles but uneven core coverage, reactive junctions and larger size extremes
molecular.overall_character: This is a reading of n-cd97f70a82cb and its actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de on the frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. The request marks both Child evaluation and Parent pairing complete; every listed trajectory exists, and no task lacks trajectories. All 4350 accepted optimizer molecules parse with RDKit. Initial observations are kept separate. Unpurchased pools, edit origins, conformers and synthesis routes were not assessed. The digest ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9460 to 0.9678 and aromatic-token presence rates from 0.9379 to 0.9667; these are fractions of SMILES carrying those features, not fractions of atoms. Most evaluated molecules therefore contain substantial ring chemistry. The principal families are substituted indole/carbonyl/aryl-nitrile assemblies, fused nitrogen heterocycles with dioxo groups, and halogenated aryl systems carrying aliphatic amines. Ordinary amides, nitriles, ethers and saturated amine rings coexist with N-halogen bonds, peroxides, unusual fused-ring graphs and very large branched products. N-halogen-bearing molecules decrease from 888 in the Parent to 516 in the Child, while molecules with at most six heavy atoms increase from 98 to 173 and those with at least fifty from 46 to 246. These are output associations, not an attribution to the learned editor or a judgement of activation. No assigned atom stereocentre is emitted, despite 1673 Child molecules having an unassigned centre. Compact leaders can look medicinally familiar, but their scores do not establish stability, stereochemical identity or makeability. Frozen scope: policy/requests/r0075-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-e05d70097d6a2084.json. Copy and input hashes: policy/scratch/r0075-00-improve-L01/molecular/input-manifest.json. Per-task descriptor evidence: policy/scratch/r0075-00-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit-summary.json. Aggregate counts and descriptor limitations: policy/scratch/r0075-00-improve-L01/molecular/aggregate-readings.json. Per-task evidence below cites every underlying Search trajectory alongside its audit; Child copies were verified byte-identical to the request-listed staging files.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted optimizer molecules have median 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. The high-score decile spans 23-26 heavy atoms and every member has three rings. It is dominated by an indole-like fused aromatic core, a carbonyl linker, a second aryl ring, methoxy/methyl substituents and often an aryl nitrile. The seed-0 leader is an ordinary secondary carboxamide with an ortho-cyanophenyl group; the seed-1 leader moves to an N-amino indole bearing an aryl ketone. These are recognisable compact heteroaromatic molecules, although the N-amino linkage needs a different stability assessment from the conventional amide. The seed-2 high family instead retains N-chlorinated amides and other heteroatom substitutions. The Child has 103 typed Murcko scaffolds across the full panel and 10 in its highest 87 molecules, versus 187 and 12 for the Parent: broad access to rings is present, but the high-score family is concentrated.
liabilities: 190 molecules contain an N-halogen bond, including 32 of the highest 87. The final structures include N-chloro and N-fluoro amides/amines, chemically different from ordinary aryl halogenation.
The N-amino ketone leader carries an N-N bond; other high examples include a sulfenate-like S-O connection. Their practical stability is unmeasured.
31 accepted molecules have at most six heavy atoms; the zero-scoring small fragments illustrate loss of the multi-group scaffold.
missing_features: Low-scoring fragments lack the aromatic-core/carbonyl/aryl-group conjunction found in the leaders; its preservation is uneven rather than globally absent.

Alternative core and linker arrangements retaining the productive nitrile/carbonyl combination are sparsely represented in the high-score set. The shown plateau does not identify a uniquely required unseen scaffold.
The trajectories do not show that more halogens or a saturated basic ring are universally needed here; those should not be inferred as objective requirements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The shared initial trimethoxy fluoroanilide scores 0.3051048084. The cyanophenyl secondary amide reaches 0.4952605565, and the N-amino/aryl-ketone analogue reaches 0.5095246654. The comparison supports the observed conjunction of a compact fused aromatic core, carbonyl and aryl nitrile; it does not isolate the effect of any one edit. Nitriles occur in 379 Child molecules versus one Parent molecule, and in 56 of the Child highest 87. The Parent leaders instead occupy substituted aryl/pyridyl amide families. Changing the methyl positions gives several amides tied at 0.4952605565; fluoromethyl and chloromethyl versions of the N-amino ketone both score 0.4888902306. Thus peripheral identity changes can leave the score flat or reduce it. The small fragment C#C scores zero. The final seed-2 N-chloroamide still scores 0.4718963173, so a high score is not a stability certificate. liabilities: The leading fluorinated carbon is bonded to two nitrogen atoms and is stereogenic without assigned configuration; its stability and stereoisomer-specific behaviour were not evaluated.

missing_features: The large branched products fail to reproduce the compact arrangement of multiple heteroaromatic blocks seen at the high end; productive connection geometry is missing more than ring count.
The Child does not cover the Parent high-score core/heteroatom arrangement at a comparable score. No single required donor, acceptor or ring can be isolated from these nonmatched structures.
A stable, stereochemically explicit alternative to the fluorinated aminal junction is not demonstrated at the same score; whether it is rewarded remains untested.

per_task.generated_character: The output is chiefly halogenated aryl chemistry combined with aliphatic amines: median 30 heavy atoms, three rings and two aromatic rings. The highest 87 molecules are a tighter 24-31-heavy-atom set, each with two aromatic rings and a match to the recorded nonaromatic trivalent ring-N predicate. The seed-1 leader combines a tertiary propyl/phenethyl amine with an azetidine ring and a thiol-substituted phenyl group. transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks reliable size-balanced changes that retain useful molecular context without either stripping it away or duplicating large assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs connected replacement and growth/shrink alternatives that preserve several useful groups together and can vary linkers without repeated-core expansion. Use only current-session feedback to learn which size changes help; these descriptive tails neither authorize a new hard size filter nor attribute the problem to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the complete accepted Search panel of n-cd97f70a82cb, 516 molecules have N-halogen bonds, 26 have O-halogen bonds and 72 have peroxide bonds. These counts are below matched Parent n-cf8d309c06de values of 888, 162 and 118, so this is a persisting limitation rather than a newly absent capability. High-score examples include fluorinated aminals, N-chlorinated amides and N-fluoro heterocycles; high score does not certify stable connection chemistry. transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional functional groups are available, but chemically credible junctions are not consistently preserved when they are combined.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Construction needs explicit local bond-environment distinctions between ordinary aryl/alkyl halogenation and heteroatom halogenation, and between stable amide/ether junctions and reactive aminal or peroxide connections. Offer chemically coherent alternatives under the same task-blind feedback rule. The observed score associations do not show that removing every flagged group would improve an objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-cd97f70a82cb, none of 4350 accepted optimizer molecules has an assigned atom stereocentre, while 1673 have an unassigned centre. Only 14 contain an atom with nonzero formal charge. One entire highest-score decile has unassigned centres; compact amine, fluorinated-ring and aminal leaders exemplify this gap. The same Search-panel Parent also has no assigned centres. Source: policy/scratch/r0075-00-improve-L01/molecular/aggregate-readings.json and policy/scratch/r0075-00-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit-summary.json. These are graph-identity observations, not measured stereoisomer or protonation effects.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic products lack explicit configuration, and charge-state coverage is sparse even in amine-rich output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly vary newly created stereochemistry and chemically plausible ionisation states as identifiable de novo construction choices. Keep canonical/isomeric identity and current-session feedback intact. Whether those additional states are useful must remain an empirical question, since the present panel does not measure their score advantage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-cd97f70a82cb clearly reaches aryl nitriles, azetidines, pyrrolidines, piperidines and piperazines; global absence of those groups would be a false diagnosis. Nevertheless, one highest-score decile contains only 13 typed/five generic scaffolds and one ring-N SMARTS match, compared with 21/ten and 58 for paired Parent n-cf8d309c06de. Its mean carbon sp3 fraction is 0.1518 versus 0.3118. Other Child high regions are broad and rich in ring N, so this is conditional coverage, not universal collapse. transferable_gaps.gap: Available nitriles and ring amines do not translate into uniformly broad coverage of useful core, saturation and linker combinations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is coherent variation of core connectivity, ring saturation and heteroatom state while retaining compatible polar and aromatic groups. Make those alternatives available to task-agnostic search and let its own accepted observations decide where they matter; do not hard-code any benchmark scaffold or force a ring-amine requirement across sessions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: n-cd97f70a82cb has 36 accepted molecules containing a perceived fully aromatic ring of four or fewer atoms, versus 170 in matched Parent n-cf8d309c06de. Ten members of one Child highest-score decile have this feature, and a separate late molecule contains a cyclic cumulated diene. These are specific inspection flags; RDKit ring perception alone does not prove a molecule cannot exist or be made. Source: policy/scratch/r0075-00-improve-L01/molecular/aggregate-readings.json and policy/scratch/r0075-00-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit-summary.json, using the same descriptors on both complete Search panels.
transferable_gaps.gap: Graph-valid ring construction still reaches strained or geometrically doubtful arrangements without establishing a credible three-dimensional structure.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring edits and core assembly need local geometric compatibility, ring-size and bond-order awareness in addition to valence validity. Provide feasible fused and partially saturated alternatives without treating the current graph descriptor as a proven synthesis filter or claiming that a geometric restriction would improve scores.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
